trust_decision.summary: Decided: on a WebSocket receive path, maxMessagePayloadSize must bound the inflated (uncompressed, reassembled) message size, not the compressed on-the-wire frame length, for every permessage-compress backend and for both the whole-message and the streaming receive API; the review is limited to that receive-side size accounting in src/autobahn/websocket/ at the pinned commit, nothing is run and no exploitation beyond the size limit is written.

landing_point.why: The single decompress_message_data() call on the receive path; an engineer reading 'permessage-deflate bypasses maxMessagePayloadSize after inflation' goes to this call and to the only existing maxMessagePayloadSize check, which runs on the compressed frame length at protocol.py:636.

fix_sites.entry_point: WebSocketServerProtocol / WebSocketClientProtocol receive path: onFrameData() after _perMessageCompress.decompress_message_data(), before _onMessageFrameData(), so both onMessage() (whole message) and onMessageFrame() (streaming) are covered
fix_sites.module_kind: core protocol module (backend-neutral, shared by twisted and asyncio adapters)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The codec-level bound (PerMessageDeflate.max_message_size, an optional knob owned by the perMessageCompressionAccept policy and defaulting to None at compress_deflate.py:755) already implements exactly the same inflation cap, so a solver can argue the correct place to fix is the permessage-deflate codec the advisory names and leave the protocol-level contract and the bzip2/snappy/brotli codecs alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A compressed message whose inflated size stays under maxMessagePayloadSize must still be delivered intact, and maxFramePayloadSize must keep bounding the compressed wire frame. Because onMessageFrameBegin() has already added the compressed frame length to message_data_total_length (protocol.py:634), the correct fix applies only the inflation delta (uncompressedLen - compressedLen); adding the full uncompressed length over-counts and falsely rejects a legitimate under-limit compressed message, and applying the inflated comparison at frame-begin would also reject frames that maxFramePayloadSize legitimately allows on the wire.

O6_input_shapes: compressed message with RSV1 set (self._isMessageCompressed True) vs plain uncompressed message, which must be untouched (fix.diff:113)
single-frame compressed message vs multi-frame fragmented compressed message, where the delta must accumulate across frames (fix.diff:114-121)
message at the limit (delivered) vs one octet over (rejected with close code 1009) - the comparison is strictly greater, matching protocol.py:636
whole-message API (onMessage) vs streaming/frame API (onMessageFrame), both reached through the same onFrameData() site
four permessage-compress backends: deflate, bzip2, snappy, brotli (src/autobahn/websocket/compress.py:60-183)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: permessage-bzip2 receive route: decompress_message_data() inflates with no cap and no cumulative accounting, so the full inflated payload is materialised before any protocol-level size test; the advisory's summary names permessage-deflate only
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory title and report name permessage-deflate; permessage-bzip2 is an optional, non-default extension whose codec is built from an accept that carries only compress levels (compress_bzip2.py:459-486), with no size option at all, so it reads as a backend that was never in scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, three modules away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: permessage-snappy receive route: snappy StreamDecompressor output is unbounded and uncounted (same sink, reached through protocol.py:1861)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Optional snappy backend with no size parameter anywhere in its offer/accept/responses; a solver can argue the advisory covers only the deflate extension.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, three modules away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: permessage-brotli receive route: brotli.Decompressor.process() output is unbounded and uncounted (same sink, reached through protocol.py:1861)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Optional brotli backend whose accept class exposes no size limit; the advisory does not mention it and brotli is not negotiated by default.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, three modules away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: client-side permessage-deflate accept: PerMessageDeflateResponseAccept carries max_message_size (compress_deflate.py:592,646) but its size cap is never derived from maxMessagePayloadSize, so a client that sets maxMessagePayloadSize gets no codec-level bound
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The response-accept is constructed by the application's perMessageCompressionAccept callable, so the size cap reads as the application's own policy rather than something the protocol option should set.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, one module away from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: bound the output inside the codec (max_length + cumulative counter) instead of the post-hoc protocol check, so the payload is never fully materialised
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The bounded-decompress machinery already exists here (added by the #1908 fix that is already in the pinned tree, src/autobahn/websocket/test/test_websocket_frame.py:113-160) and only needs to be fed the protocol's limit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: wrap decompress_message_data() in try/except PayloadExceededError and turn it into _max_message_size_exceeded(close 1009)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The deflate codec raises PayloadExceededError against its own max_message_size (compress_deflate.py:836-840) and nothing on the receive path catches it, so an opt-in codec cap currently escapes as an uncaught exception out of _dataReceived instead of failing the connection.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: round-trip max_message_size through __json__ in the accept/serializer objects
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PerMessageDeflateOfferAccept.__json__ already emits max_message_size (compress_deflate.py:421) while PerMessageDeflateResponseAccept.__json__ (655-661) and PerMessageDeflate.__json__ (766-774) omit it, so any config/telemetry round-trip silently loses the only inflation cap - a natural sibling for a maintainer hardening this area.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a maxMessagePayloadSize option on the rawsocket batched transport that enforces its own MAX_LENGTH
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same option name already exists on a second, non-WebSocket transport with its own message-size limit, so a maintainer extending message-size accounting across transports would add the guard there too.

O9_family: Improper handling of highly compressed data / unbounded resource allocation on decompression - decompression bomb (CWE-409, CWE-770)

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend (pyproject.toml:3), pip/uv; optional C extensions for snappy/brotli (brotlicffi on PyPy, pyproject.toml optional-dependencies); Twisted and asyncio backends
O10_build.project_tests: src/autobahn/websocket/test/test_websocket_protocol.py drives the protocol directly over autobahn.testutil.FakeTransport (offline), and src/autobahn/websocket/test/test_websocket_frame.py:88-163 covers the PerMessageDeflate max_message_size cap added by the already-applied #1908 fix; the published fix adds src/autobahn/websocket/test/test_websocket_max_message_size.py, which is absent at the pinned commit. The wstest conformance suite needs a live peer and is not part of the offline story.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Fix inside the permessage-deflate codec named by the report - set PerMessageDeflate.max_message_size from maxMessagePayloadSize or add the check in decompress_message_data() (compress_deflate.py:819) - which leaves bzip2/snappy/brotli unbounded and does not honour the protocol-level maxMessagePayloadSize contract.
